title: The Whole Counsel of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The whole counsel of God means that God’s people must receive, teach, and obey all that God has revealed in Scripture, not only selected portions that feel easy, familiar, or preferred. Faithfulness requires honoring the full message of God’s Word.
summary: The whole counsel of God means that God’s people must receive, teach, and obey all that God has revealed in Scripture, not only selected portions that feel easy, familiar, or preferred. Faithfulness requires honoring the full message of God’s Word.
christFocus: Christ is revealed through the whole counsel of God. His person, work, kingdom, promises, warnings, mercy, judgment, and glory must be proclaimed according to all Scripture, not a reduced or selective message.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God has spoken more than a few favorite truths. The whole counsel of God includes creation, sin, judgment, promise, covenant, law, wisdom, prophecy, Gospel, grace, repentance, holiness, suffering, mission, resurrection, and eternal hope.

Faithful teaching does not hide hard truths or overemphasize only comfortable ones. God’s people need promises and warnings, comfort and correction, doctrine and application, mercy and holiness, grace and obedience.

Paul could say he was innocent of blood because he did not shrink back from declaring the whole counsel of God. This shows that partial teaching can be spiritually dangerous when it avoids truths people need to hear.

The whole counsel of God keeps the church balanced and healthy. It guards against shallow encouragement, harsh legalism, empty speculation, selective obedience, and doctrine shaped by cultural preference rather than Scripture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People naturally prefer parts of Scripture that comfort them and may avoid parts that confront them. Churches can drift by preaching only what attracts attention, avoids offense, or fits a narrow emphasis. Over time, selective teaching produces shallow disciples.

This doctrine calls the church back to faithful fullness. God’s people need all that God has spoken because He knows what forms, warns, heals, corrects, and strengthens His people.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not build your faith on selected favorite verses while ignoring the rest of God’s Word. Read, receive, and obey Scripture widely and humbly. When teaching or discipling others, do not avoid necessary truths because they are difficult. Trust that all God has spoken is good, wise, and needed.
